lab.title: Answer three questions without a browser
lab.scenario: Use only the terminal. The goal is not to memorize flags; it is to build the reflex to look them up.

steps.text: Read the synopsis of cp and find the option that preserves timestamps and mode.
steps.verify: Look for -p, --preserve. The synopsis should make sense now.

steps.text: Read the fstab file-format page and find the sixth field.
steps.verify: The sixth field controls fsck pass order; root is usually 1, others 2 or 0.

steps.text: Search manual descriptions for the word "quota".
steps.verify: You should see several administration and file-format pages.

steps.text: Find out which installed package owns sshd.
steps.verify: command -v sshd should print a path such as /usr/sbin/sshd, and rpm -qf should name openssh-server.

steps.text: Locate the local documentation directory for a package you have installed.
steps.verify: The directory should exist under /usr/share/doc and contain the package documentation.

quiz.q: Which command reads the file format of /etc/passwd rather than the passwd command?
quiz.why: Section 5 contains file formats. man 5 passwd describes the colon-separated passwd file.

options: Searches manual page descriptions by keyword
quiz.why: man -k (apropos) searches the whatis index by keyword. The index must exist for results to appear.

quiz.q: How do you find the installed package that owns /usr/bin/ls?
quiz.why: rpm -qf queries the RPM database for the owning package. dnf provides is for packages that are available but not necessarily installed.
